text:
ConocoPhillips fell 4.7% today after oil prices dropped on news that a damaged Saudi pipeline will restart operations within days. The U.S. had said the pipeline was disabled, forcing Saudi Arabia to route exports through the Red Sea; its reopening reduces the near-term supply tightness that had been supporting prices. Brent crude sits at $109.51 per barrel versus WTI at $97.26, and that softening hit the stock hard despite diesel fuel hitting record highs of $6.31 per gallon — a sign that refining margins may tighten even as crude weakens.

The broader geopolitical backdrop — including a Houthi drone strike on Mecca and ongoing tensions over the Strait of Hormuz — had been underpinning crude values, but the pipeline restart announcement shifted the risk calculus. Meanwhile, a new Venezuelan oil development by a rival explorer could add supply pressure longer term, compounding today's immediate crude-price headwind.
